about: Argyle was founded in 1987 by Rollin Soles, who had recognised in the late 1970s that the cool Willamette Valley could grow Chardonnay and Pinot Noir to rival Champagne. The first winery was a converted hazelnut-drying barn in the small town of Dundee, which today is Argyle’s tasting house; production moved to a larger facility in nearby Newberg in 2014. Argyle is the only Willamette winery that Wine Spectator has consistently placed among its Top 100 Wines of the World in all three categories: red, white and sparkling.

The estate farms more than 400 acres across three vineyards in the Dundee Hills and Eola-Amity Hills, with each block tended for either still or sparkling wine depending on the year. Its vineyards are LIVE Certified Sustainable. The Willamette Valley Pinot Noir is the winery’s broadest red, drawing on fruit from across the valley to show the house style rather than a single site. The 2023 comes in at 13.8% alcohol. Expect dark cherry, red raspberry and orange zest, with black tea and spice on the palate. The previous vintage, the 2022, earned 92 points from Wine Spectator.
